title: A Stop then a clear or cancel during an in-flight create reopens the proposal for a second paid render
body:
## Summary
After Stop, a Suno record whose create is still spending reads `queued`, so clearSunoQueue (and cancelJob) cancel it and its kernel job; the proposal then reads as a candidate and can be queued and rendered again.

## Description
setSunoQueue(false) (lib/sound/suno/queue.ts) pauses every queued or running kernel job (lib/producers/suno.ts pauseSunoJobs; kernel job.ts `pause` moves a running job to `paused` at once while the step in flight finishes) and rewrites the record `active -> queued`, deleting phase and model. clearSuno (lib/sound/suno/store.ts:255-263) cancels any record in `queued`; clearSunoQueue then cancels the kernel job in `paused`. cancelJob reads the overlay, where paused maps to `queued`, so it allows the same. The create completes, its clips land on a cancelled record, and isCandidate (store.ts:165-168) admits the proposal again: enqueueIn mints a new job whose id has no clips, so both models are created a second time. Built and DEMOTED this round: skipping kernel jobs in state `running` does not help, because a paused job with a step in flight is indistinguishable from an idle paused one in the kernel's job row. Fixed needs a 'step in flight' signal - the lane slot still held by the job, or the record's phase kept through Stop - read inside the store lock by both clearSunoQueue and cancelJob.

## Flow
- enqueue + launch a live job; driveSuno with FAKE_SUNO.hold set; wait for the create call
- setSunoQueue(false)
- clearSunoQueue({ jobIds: [job] }) -> { cancelled: 1 } today (want cancelled 0, skipped 1)
- enqueueProposals([proposal], { launch: false }) -> a NEW job id today (want the same live job)

## Expected impact
The operator cannot pay Suno twice for one proposal by clearing or cancelling a stopped column while a create runs. Could break: a clear/cancel issued in that window is refused until the create lands.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a create in flight is never cancelled into a second paid render
Before: case red: clearSunoQueue cancelled 1, re-enqueue minted a second job (vitest, producer-suno.test.ts, fake driver, no credits)
After: predicted cancelled 0 / skipped 1 / same job id; a running-only busy check measured NOT enough (still cancelled 1)
Method: gate - the instrument was built and run red; the fix needs a kernel-side in-flight signal outside this round's paths (lib/producers/suno.ts, packages/kernel)
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
lib/sound/suno/store.ts:255-263 cancels any `queued` record
lib/sound/suno/queue.ts:273-283 Stop rewrites active -> queued
lib/producers/suno.ts:241-249 pause on running jobs
packages/kernel/src/job.ts:292-298 pause moves a running job to paused at once
measured: the case below, red with the overlay-running fix applied
instrument: tests/next-server/producer-suno.test.ts case 'a clear never cancels a job whose create is in flight, so its proposal is not queued a second time' (hold the fake create, Stop, clearSunoQueue -> expect cancelled 0 skipped 1, re-enqueue returns the same job id, then release and cancelJob to clean up); red today; run with --testTimeout=30000 under load

title: Three SoundError-to-AppError maps on the audio desk disagree on 409, 500 and a non-SoundError
body:
## Summary
huntDesk.ts, lessons.ts and rubric.ts each turn a thrown SoundError into an AppError code with their own table, and the tables disagree.

## Description
lib/sound/huntDesk.ts:34-43: 400 invalid, 404 not-found, 409 conflict, 502/503 unavailable, else internal; a non-SoundError -> unavailable. lib/sound/lessons.ts:45-52: 404, 400, 409 conflict, else unavailable (so a SoundError 500 - the corrupt-store refusal - is unavailable here and internal at the other two); a non-SoundError -> internal. lib/sound/rubric.ts:249-271: 409 -> refused (conflict at the other two), 403 refused, 503 unavailable, else internal; non-SoundError -> internal. One sound store throws the same errors to all three. Fixed: one exported mapper beside SoundError, read by the three doors.

## Flow
- a store write that throws SoundError(409) -> conflict on a crown, conflict on a lesson, refused on a score
- an fs EIO -> unavailable on a crown, internal on a lesson or a score

## Expected impact
The desk's islands render a code per door; one store error reads the same everywhere. Could break: a client that branches on rubric's `refused` for a 409.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one mapping
Before: 3 tables; 3 of 6 sampled inputs (409, 500, Error) map differently
After: predicted 1 table, 0 disagreements
Method: probe - the three tables read side by side; not built: the canonical choice (409 conflict vs refused) and its consumers in app/(studio)/audio need a reviewer, and the shared home (lib/sound/store.ts) is sound-generation-engine's
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/sound/huntDesk.ts:34 STATUS
lib/sound/lessons.ts:49 inStore ternary
lib/sound/rubric.ts:249 STATUS_CODE
instrument: a vitest table case: SoundError(400/404/409/500/503) and new Error('EIO') through each door's mapper (export them), assert one code per input

title: A Floor sentence's Suno prompt sees fewer of its lane's examples than a lane draft does
body:
## Summary
proposeFromSentence builds its examples from the lane's proposals only; proposeSuno adds the lane's job styles too.

## Description
lib/sound/suno/propose.ts proposeSuno: examples = proposals of the lane (newest first) + f.jobs of the lane's fields.style, deduped, cut to 8. proposeFromSentence: proposals only. A job keeps its own snapshot of fields and outlives a deleted proposal (store.ts deleteProposal), so a lane whose rendered prompts were cleared from Proposed shows them to a lane draft and hides them from a sentence draft - the sentence turn may repeat what was already rendered. Fixed: one laneExamples(f, lane) read by both.

## Flow
- a lane with a done job whose proposal was deleted
- proposeSuno prompt EXAMPLES lists that style; sentencePrompt EXAMPLES says (none yet)

## Expected impact
The Floor's Suno turn varies from what was rendered as the lane draft does. Could break: nothing visible beyond the prompt text.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one examples rule
Before: 2 spellings of the lane's examples, differing on job styles
After: 1
Method: simulation - walked over propose.ts; the instrument is a pure prompt probe with a canned ReasonFn, not built for budget
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: suno.json with a lane job and no proposal; capture both prompts through a canned ReasonFn; assert both EXAMPLES carry the job's style

title: A corrupt knowledge/audio/params.json is read as 'nothing measured yet'
body:
## Summary
readAudioParams catches every error, so an unparseable params.json briefs the next hunt as if no strength were measured.

## Description
lib/sound/hunt.ts readAudioParams: `try { JSON.parse(await readFile(...)) } catch { return null }`. Its own comment says only an ABSENT file means 'nothing measured yet', which the prompt is told to read as permission to explore. A truncated or merge-conflicted generated file takes the same path silently. Fixed: ENOENT -> null; anything else is a SoundError naming the file and `npx tsx pipeline/sound.mts knowledge` (or a named line on the draft).

## Flow
- write '{' to knowledge/audio/params.json
- draft a hunt: the STRENGTHS slot says none yet, no error anywhere

## Expected impact
A broken generated file is seen instead of steering every hunt to explore. Could break: a hunt draft refused until the file is regenerated.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a swallowed error named
Before: error paths swallowed 2 of 2 (ENOENT and parse)
After: 1 of 2 (ENOENT only, by design)
Method: simulation - the path is cwd-relative to the tracked file; a probe needs a path seam (SOUND_KNOWLEDGE_DIR) the reader does not take
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: read params through SOUND_KNOWLEDGE_DIR (the probe already sets it); a case with '{' in the file expects a 500 naming it, red today

title: A blob path the store refuses is never recorded, so the measure pass retries it every run
body:
## Summary
measureMissing records a decoder refusal as a row but not a blobs.pathOf refusal, so that blob is wanted again on every run and a limit's worth of them starves the pass.

## Description
lib/sound/measureRun.ts measureMissing: `if (!file.ok) { failed.push(...); continue; }` writes no audio_measures row, while a decode failure writes one ('a fact too, so it is not decoded again'). measuresMissing (packages/kernel/src/library/measures.ts:86-97) returns the first `limit` unmeasured shas with no ORDER BY, so `limit` such rows are returned forever. pathOf refuses only a non-sha256 media_sha (packages/kernel/src/blob.ts:70-73), which a library_docs row could carry from an import. Fixed: write the refusal as an error row like the decode case.

## Flow
- a library_docs row with media_sha 'not-a-sha' and decodable media_facts
- measureMissing(limit 1) twice: measured 0, failed 1 both times; a valid blob behind it never measured

## Expected impact
The free media-facts job makes progress past a bad row. Could break: putAudioMeasures may refuse a non-sha key (check its schema first).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no starvation
Before: pathOf refusals recorded 0 of 1
After: 1 of 1
Method: simulation - needs a kernel library fixture with a bad sha; not built for budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/sound/measureRun.ts measureMissing pathOf branch
packages/kernel/src/library/measures.ts:86-97 LIMIT with no ORDER BY
instrument: tests/next-server/audio-measure.test.ts: seed a bad-sha library doc ahead of a good one, run measureMissing(limit 1) twice, expect the good blob measured on run 2; red today

title: The measure pass records RMS but no loudness or true peak, so technical acceptance has no gate
body:
## Summary
lib/sound/measure.ts measures peaks, RMS energy, length, tempo and key; generated-music-acceptance's technical gate is loudness at the destination target and true peak under the ceiling, which nothing in the studio measures.

## Description
media-generation/audio-generation/generated-music-acceptance (golden path, 'Measurement is the spine'; technique loudness-and-peak-acceptance): what the plan committed to numbers is measured - duration, section offsets, LUFS, dBTP - and 'unmeasured is not pass'. measureSignal returns energy as RMS 0..1 (not LUFS) and no peak in dBTP; the kept/rejected verdict therefore clears a take whose loudness nobody checked. A real build adds integrated LUFS and true peak to the measure (ffmpeg ebur128 in the same decode, or a K-weighted pass in measure.ts), a column on audio_measures, and an acceptance reading on the take.

## Flow
- a take renders 6 LU hotter than its siblings
- it is kept on the Board; no reading on it or in the Library says so

## Expected impact
Generated cues land at consistent loudness for the destination. Could break: a schema change on audio_measures (kernel library).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - loudness acceptance exists
Before: loudness/peak readings per take 0
After: 2 (LUFS-I, dBTP)
Method: simulation - a new measurement capability with a kernel schema change; outside the context's declared scope (it measures, but names no acceptance gate)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
lib/sound/measure.ts AudioMeasure {peaks, energy, durationS, tempoBpm, key}
